 Warehouse
Account of the Indian Commissioner at Regina.

As you are aware, $21,700 has been deposited to the credit of the Receiver General. No special fund can be created
without the authority of Parliament, and this has not yet been obtained. I will draw my Minister's attention to the
closing paragraph of your letter, which refers to the necessity for special parliamentary authority in this regard.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, DS.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Regina Warehouse Account: Inquiry as to Stock-taking


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 26, 1924.

SIR, - In the report submitted to me by Mr. J.W. Reid of this office on his examination during the summer of 1923,
into Mr. W.M. Graham's Warehouse Account, he states as follows: -

"I learned that no regular stock-taking had been made since February, 1921, and as since that date a large quantity of
goods has been received at and issued from the Warehouse, there are likely to be considerable discrepancies, although
I would judge the warehouse man to be competent and trustworthy man. I recommended to Mr. Graham that complete
stock-taking be made as soon as possible, by responsible officers, that all worthless articles be destroyed by them and
written off, and that the stock books be adjusted to the result of such stock-taking; and that, after the actual stock on
hand has thus been established, test audits of the stock-in-hand be made at frequent intervals by checking each time a
number of items taken at random."



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 585-588) ===
<!-- page 585 -->
I should like to be informed as to whether a complete check of the stock in the Regina Warehouse has been made since
Mr. Reid's visit of inspection, and

<!-- page 586 -->
if such has been done please send a copy of any report that may have been made in connection therewith. If such
check of the stock has not yet been made I would suggest that Mr. Graham be requested to have a complete
verification of the stock made at the earliest possible date.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

NOTE. - No reply had been received to the above letter up to the time of printing.

Regina Warehouse Account: Amounts due by Employees and Others for Goods Purchased


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 27, 1924.

SIR, - The books of account in connection with Mr. Graham's Warehouse Account. at Regina, which were examined
during the summer of 1923 by Mr. Reid of this office, showed that, in addition to a number of Indian agencies that
were charged with the value of goods sent them for sale to the Indians, a number of Indian schools and of individuals
were indebted for goods supplied them.

A number of these accounts have since been settled but there still remain a considerable number which so far as I can
determine from the receipts, were not settled by the close of the fiscal year. A list of these accounts which appeared on
the books on June 30, 1923, and which appear to be still unsettled accompanies this letter; a number of the names
appearing on this list are those of employees of your department at Regina.

I should like to have a report from Mr. Graham on these outstanding accounts, showing why they have not been
settled. I have also to ask for a list of outstanding accounts as on March 31, 1924.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.



NOTE. - No reply had been received to the above letter up to the time of printing,

Indian Trust Fund, Province of Quebec Fund: Payment of longstanding Charges for Relief Supplies


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, April 3, 1924.

SIR, - Indian Trust Fund cheque No. 6732 issued on January 8th, 1924, and charged against the Province of Quebec,
Fund is for the payment of $1,500 to J.T. Guite, Limited, of Maria, P.Q. "In full settlement of claim of supplies
furnished Indians. of Maria, P.Q."

The documents furnished in support of this claim consist of a, number of typewritten copies of statements on, your
departmental form, evidently prepared in your department or in the Indian office, at Maria. These statements how in

<!-- page 587 -->
detail the supplies, claimed to have been issued during the years, 1918, 1919, 1920 and 1921 to various individual
Indians, of the Maria Indian Band. The, total amount of the statements is $2,170.05 which may be summarized as
follows.: -

<!-- page 588 -->
Emergency Medical Relief $ 84 49
Emergency Clothing Relief 665 97
Emergency Food Relief     1,419 59
...                       $2,170 05

Each separate statement bear's the following certificates,


"Certified Correct
Charges, fair and just,
J.D. CHÉNÉ,
Departmental Engineer."

From the fact of these statements being certified to by Mr. Chéné, I infer that he was instructed by you to investigated
this claim, although his, duties as departmental engineer would not ordinarily call upon him to make inquiries of this
nature.

In connection with this, payment, I should like to be fully informed on the following points: - (1) Under what authority
and on whose responsibility were there supplies furnished the Indians (2) What evidence is there that these goods were
actually received by the Indians. (3) What legal claim, if any had J.T. Guite;, Ltd., against your department for the
goods Supplied by him. (4) What application, if any, was received from J.T. Guite, Ltd., for payment for these
supplies. (5) What evidence is, there that no part of this claim bad been previously paid, either by your department or
otherwise. (6) On what basis was the amount of $1,500 as settlement in full arrived at.

In this connection I should like to be furnished with a copy of any report that may have been submitted by Mr. Chéné.


I am, sir, your obedient Servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, May 13, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I have to refer to your letter of the 3rd ultimo with, regard to the payment by this Department of an
amount of $1,500 to Messrs. Guite & Co., general merchants of Maria, Quebec, for relief supplied to Indians of that
reserve between 1918 and 1921. This, firm submitted their accounts to the Department from time to time. In view of
the fact that the Indian Agent had not reported on the. matter it was considered necessary to have. a careful
investigation. Accordingly Mr. Chéné was sent to Maria for that purpose, being specialty qualified therefor as a
bilinguist. He found that the supplies in question were issued to the Indians, for the most part, under emergency
conditions during the successive epidemic of influenza. I am not aware of any legal status. that Messrs. Guite would
have as against the Department with respect to these accounts. It is clear, however, that it was absolutely necessary that
the supplies, should be issued in order to alleviate distress, and to save the lives of the Indians who were sick and
destitute. The Department, therefore, could not view the matter in its strictly legal aspect, being concerned rather with
the urgency of the conditions. In checking over the accounts Mr. Chéné passed only those items which seemed
absolutely necessary. These the Department feels, morally bound to recognize. It was with this proper discrimination
that the amount of $1,500 was arrived at. The records of the
